screening_questions.tell_me_about_yourself: I am a third-year Software Engineering student at the University of Calgary, graduating May 2027. I have almost a decade of coding experience across full-stack development, ML evaluation, and cloud tools. I currently evaluate 200+ AI model outputs weekly at Alignerr and lead a 10-person software team at the University of Calgary Solar Racing team. I am looking for a Summer 2026 internship where I can work on hard engineering problems and ship real software.
screening_questions.strengths: My strongest technical skill is building reliable backend systems. I design for failure from the start, write tests before considering a feature done, and make the system observable so problems are diagnosable. I also communicate well between technical and non-technical stakeholders. And I am fast: I pick up new tools and frameworks quickly and I do not stay stuck.
screening_questions.weakness: I used to spend too long polishing details before sharing early work. I have learned to show progress sooner, collect feedback earlier, and iterate in tighter loops.
screening_questions.challenge: During the Solar Racing team's first competition with the telemetry system I built, the alerting system was firing false positives. During a race, that is dangerous. I had built structured logging into the ingestion pipeline, so I traced the bad alerts back to a sensor calibration issue rather than a software bug. I wrote a filtering layer that normalized the outlier readings and the false positives stopped. The team finished top 10 at FSGP 2024.
screening_questions.career_goals: Long term, I want to grow into an engineer who can own important systems end-to-end and make strong technical decisions in high-trust environments. In the near term, I want to sharpen the exact skills this role demands most and learn from engineers who already operate at a high level.
screening_questions.favourite_project: My favourite project is the Real-Time Telemetry System I built for the University of Calgary Solar Racing team. It streams 50+ live sensor signals per second with sub-100ms latency and includes anomaly detection that surfaces critical issues within 2 seconds. I built it in Python with WebSockets and PostgreSQL, with Grafana dashboards the team used in real competition conditions. The system contributed to a top-10 finish at Formula Sun Grand Prix 2024.
